messages.author: 35d5f8048b3f3662
messages.subject: group / cluster size from dht2()
parts:
Hi Distance Group,

I've MCDS modelled spatially replicated surveys to derive density using dht2(). Observations are of clusters and I beleive the dht2() output also describes clusters. I would like help to derive average cluster size so that I can get an abundance estimate for individuals (if this is possible in a replicate scenario)?

Below is an example of my flatfiling and dht2'ing and fro'ing.

# make a flatfile useful for dht2 to model MCDS
flatfile.mcds <- data.frame(object = front.data$object, distance = front.data$distance, Sample.Label = front.data$Sample.Label,
                          Region.Label = front.data$Region.Label, Rep = front.data$replicate)

flatfile.mcds <- left_join(flatfile.mcds, region.data)
flatfile.mcds <- left_join(flatfile.mcds, final.samples)

# make a covariate data frame to join to flatfile
mcds.covars <- data.frame(object = front.data$object, obsname = front.data$obsname, side = front.data$side)

# Now join covariates to flatfile using object.
flatfile.mcds <- left_join(flatfile.mcds, mcds.covars)

# Compute abundance estimates over FG, "Flats" Region.

FG.roo.MCDS <- dht2(ddf = MCDS.25,
                        flatfile = flatfile.mcds,
                        stratification = "effort_sum",
                        strat_formula = ~Rep,
                        ci_width = 0.95)
FG.roo.MCDS

Thank you,
Evan

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] group / cluster size from dht2()
parts:
Evan

Good to hear from you again.

I have to confess, I've not used dht2​ with objects that occur in groups. However, I altered one of the data sets that ships with the Distance package minke​ to create a size​ field. After fitting a detection function and using dht2​, I printed the resulting object summary. The estimates produced by dht2​ are for numbers of individuals, not numbers of groups. Average group size and variability in group size is also generated in the output.  This appears to hold regardless of the value of the stratification​ argument to dht2.  See below.

library(Distance)
data(minke)
library(dsims)
minke$size <- dsims:::rztpois(dim(minke)[1], 2)  # manufacture a group size
minke.trunc <- 1.5
minke.df.all <- ds(minke, truncation=minke.trunc, key="hr", adjustment=NULL)
summary(minke.df.all)
usingdht2 <- dht2(ddf=minke.df.all, flatfile=minke,
                  strat_formula=~Region.Label, stratification="geographical")
print(usingdht2)

minke$Area <- minke$Area[1]
minke.df.all <- ds(minke, truncation=minke.trunc, key="hr", adjustment=NULL)
summary(minke.df.all)
test <- dht2(ddf=minke.df.all, flatfile=minke,
             strat_formula=~Region.Label, stratification="replicate")
print(test)

I'm not sure using effort_sum​ is the best form of the stratification argument, if your surveys are replicates, then specify replicate​ as the value of the argument.  Hope that helps.

Evan

I forgot you were a ddf​ ninja.  I've added a few lines of code to the code I sent previously to check for correspondence between dht​ and dht2​ output with the "toy" minke whale data set when using region, sample and observation tables. I see agreement between the two analyses when formulated this way

minkddf <- ddf(dsmodel=~mcds(key="hr", formula=~Region.Label),
               method="ds",
               data=minke, meta.data = list(width=minke.trunc))
reg <- data.frame(Region.Label=c("South", "North"), Area=c(84734, 84734))
sam <- data.frame(Region.Label=c(rep("South", 13), rep("North", 12)),
                  Sample.Label=seq(1,25),
                  Effort=unique(minke$Effort)))
minkddfdht <- dht(minkddf, region.table=reg, sample.table=sam,
                  options=list(varflag=0,group=TRUE), se=TRUE)
print(minkddfdht)
obso <- minke[ , c("object", "Sample.Label", "size")]
minkddfdht2 <- dht2(minkddf, observations = obso,
                    transects = sam,
                    geo_strat = reg, strat_formula = ~Region.Label)
print(minkddfdht2)

Hi Eric 

😂 I think I'll put 'ddf ninja' on my resume - although after reading this it may become apparent I'm only on my yellow belt!

I've described the study to you incorrectly, very sorry but I've sent you down the wrong path here. I said it was 'spatially' replicated but I think the samples should be treated as temporally replicated. We sampled the same study region 11 times over 3 days with a coverage of ~ 20% for each replicate. This is why I'd specified the "effort_sum" stratification argument. The alternative argument "replicate" gives the same abundance estimate

I had some trouble recreating the situation witht the minke example you sent. So I've included my model for you to reference instead.

Just to recap my problem - I suspect dht2() is giving me an estimate for groups rather than individuals in this particular situation. It may be related to temporal stratification.

# AIC chosen model
MCDS.25 <- ddf(data=front.data, dsmodel = ~mcds(key="hn", formula = ~side+obsname),
     meta.data=list(binned=TRUE,point=FALSE,width=300,breaks=c(0,50,100,200,300))

# make a flatfile useful for dht2 to model MCDS

# Compute abundance estimates over FG, "Flats" Region.

                        flatfile = flatfile.mcds,

Evan (yikes: I thought I had sent this on 04Oct23)

Yes, it seems we are "talking past" each other. Perhaps we might want to take this conversation "off-list" until I better understand the problem. This is my current understanding:
  • estimated abundance coming out of dht2​ are too small
    • specifically you imply dht() 'Abundance Estimate for Clusters' = dht2() 'Total Abundance Estimate'
  • you suspect this may be caused by the temporal replication of surveys in your design
  • I've tried to duplicate your scenario with a simple data set provided in the Distance​ package
